The change adds a new refusal. If a test failed on its first try and passed only when it was rerun, the repin is now refused, even though the test run as a whole is reported as passing. This is stricter than before: a run that used to count as "tests pass" (examples EX-5, EX-6 and EX-17) no longer allows a repin.

It's unclear whether this was wanted. The prompt logged for that turn is an unrelated message about recording a post-merge proof and doesn't ask for this. The change also isn't plainly wrong: a test that only passes on a rerun may be hiding a real failure. Whether "tests pass" should include passing only on a rerun is your decision, so it isn't being sent back on a guess.

The change adds a stricter rule to the repin check. If a test fails on its first try and passes only when rerun, the check now counts that as a failure, so the link is not repinned. The case stays open and goes on to be rerun or fixed. Before the change, a pass on the rerun was enough.

You haven't said whether a test that passes only on a rerun counts as "tests pass". The comment in the code argues for the stricter rule: a test that fails on every first try is not just flaky. Nothing in the turn that likely made this change asked for it, though. That message was about recording another requirement's proof. Since this could be a deliberate tightening or an unwanted side effect, it shouldn't be undone on a guess.
